2 East 67 Street co-op and the pied-à-terre tax line

The city values 2 East 67 Street (15 apartments) at $27.99 million, an average of $1.87 million per apartment, above the $1 million line for New York City's pied-à-terre surcharge. Each apartment's figure depends on its shares, and whether it owes the surcharge depends on who lives there.

How a co-op apartment's value is set for the surcharge

The city values a co-op as one building. For the surcharge, an apartment's value is its share of that building value, based on the shares the apartment holds in the corporation. The roll does not publish shares, so the figure above is a plain average: apartments with more shares sit above it, smaller ones below. The building value also covers any shops or offices in it, which can lift the average. Use the co-op share calculator to test an exact share fraction.

For condos and co-ops, the Phase 1 surcharge (July 2026 to June 2028) starts at $1 million and applies to the whole value: 4% up to $3 million, 5.25% up to $5 million and 6.5% above. It is not owed when the apartment is the primary residence of the owner, the owner's spouse, child, parent, sibling, grandparent or grandchild, or a tenant on an arm's-length lease of at least one year (see the exemptions guide). The roll does not show residency, so this page does not say who pays.

How the city valued the building

State law has DOF value co-ops as if they were rental buildings: it estimates the rent the building would earn, using comparable rental buildings, subtracts expenses and converts the net income into a value. The rental-comparables guide explains the method.

In its latest published record (report year 2022), DOF valued the building at $26.86 million, an implied capitalization rate of 12.5%, using 3 comparable rental buildings. The FY2027 Notice of Property Value lists the current figures.

The building summary lists DOF's income and expense figures and the comparable rental buildings it used, with units near each line and recorded sales. Or inspect a 2-page Sample Unit Report ($79 PDF).

Deadline to challenge the value

An owner who wants to contest the market value behind the surcharge files Tax Commission Form TC107 by March 1, 2027 for condos and co-ops. A co-op corporation may file for a unit owner. The form cannot be used to protest the assessed value. The TC107 guide covers the grounds and the filing steps.
